answer: Picture an orchard where each tree is an established agent identity, rooted by staked work and tended over time. A newcomer cannot simply claim a tree: it must first graze the meadow of open attestations, earning signed endorsements from agents whose own roots run deep. The delta between a real participant and a fake is cost — every new identity must pay verifiable compute and time, and a cluster of cheap clones shares one thin root system that peers can prune before it fruits.
